q: Pseudo-random numbers from a fixed seed are reproducible.
why: Fact. The generator is deterministic: same seed, same sequence.

q: Which is the recommended way to get random numbers in modern numpy?
o: rng = np.random.default_rng(seed) and pass rng around
why: An explicit Generator is isolated from other code's draws and reproducible.

q: Eight workers all use default_rng(1). What happens?
o: they repeat the same runs, and the MCSE is about √8 too small
why: All workers produce identical draws, so there are only one worker's worth of distinct runs.

q: With 9 workers all using the same seed, by what factor is the reported MCSE too small?
why: There is only 1/9 of the claimed runs, so the true error is √9 = 3× the reported one.

q: How do you give 16 workers independent streams from one recorded number?
o: reuse one generator in all processes
why: spawn derives statistically independent child seeds from one parent seed.

q: Trying seeds until the new strategy wins, then reporting that run, is fine if the code is correct.
why: Myth. Choosing the seed by its result is cherry-picking, like p-hacking.

q: Common random numbers help most when you estimate …
o: a difference between two similar scenarios
why: Shared draws make the noise mostly cancel in the difference.

q: CRN cut the MCSE of a difference from 1.03 to 0.40. About how many times more independent runs would match it?
why: Runs scale with the variance ratio: (1.03/0.40)² ≈ 6.6.

q: Python's random module is suitable for generating security tokens.
why: False. Use the secrets module; simulation generators are predictable by design.
